## Problem 

What is the expected value of the highest roll of a $6$-sided die if we roll it until we get a $4$?

## Analytical Solution

Define the [[stochastic-processes|stochastic process]] $\{X_t\}_{t\geq 1}$
with independent [[discrete-uniform-distribution|discrete uniform]] rolls
$X_t\sim\mathcal{U}(\{1,\ldots,6\})$. Further define the running maximum

$$
S_t = \max\{X_1,\ldots,X_t\},
$$

and the [[stopping-times|stopping time]]
$\tau = \min\{t\geq 1: X_t = 4\}$. We include the final roll of $4$, so
$S_\tau\in\{4,5,6\}$. We wish to compute $\mathbb{E}[S_\tau]$.

By the [[law-of-total-expectation]],

$$
\begin{align*}
\mathbb{E}[S_\tau]
&= \mathbb{E}\left[\mathbb{E}[S_\tau\mid\tau]\right] \\
&= \sum_{t=1}^{\infty}
\underbrace{\mathbb{E}[S_t\mid\tau=t]}_{(1)}
\underbrace{\mathbb{P}(\tau=t)}_{(2)}.
\end{align*}
$$

For (2), $\tau$ follows a [[geometric-distribution|geometric distribution]]
(number of trials to get one success) with success probability $p=1/6$:

$$
\mathbb{P}(\tau=t) = \left(\frac{5}{6}\right)^{t-1}\frac{1}{6}.
$$

For (1), the tail-sum formula gives

$$
\mathbb{E}[S_t\mid\tau=t]
= \sum_{s=0}^{5}\mathbb{P}(S_t>s\mid\tau=t).
$$

For $s\in\{0,1,2,3\}$, each probability is $1$ because the final roll is
$4$. For $s\in\{4,5\}$, we use [[order-statistics]]. Conditional on
$\tau=t$, the first $t-1$ rolls are independent and uniform on
$\{1,2,3,5,6\}$, while $X_t=4$. Conditioning only on $X_t=4$ would not
exclude earlier rolls of $4$. Hence

$$
\begin{align*}
\mathbb{P}(S_t\leq s\mid\tau=t)
&= \prod_{i=1}^{t-1}\mathbb{P}(X_i\leq s\mid X_i\neq 4) \\
&= \left(\frac{s-1}{5}\right)^{t-1}.
\end{align*}
$$

Taking complements and returning to (1),

$$
\begin{align*}
\mathbb{E}[S_t\mid\tau=t]
&= 4 + \left[1-\left(\frac{3}{5}\right)^{t-1}\right]
       + \left[1-\left(\frac{4}{5}\right)^{t-1}\right] \\
&= 6-\left(\frac{3}{5}\right)^{t-1}
    -\left(\frac{4}{5}\right)^{t-1}.
\end{align*}
$$

For example, when $t=1$ this is $4$, as expected. Substituting into the
original sum and evaluating the geometric series,

$$
\begin{align*}
\mathbb{E}[S_\tau]
&= \frac{1}{6}\sum_{t=1}^{\infty}
\left[
6\left(\frac{5}{6}\right)^{t-1}
-\left(\frac{1}{2}\right)^{t-1}
-\left(\frac{2}{3}\right)^{t-1}
\right] \\
&= \frac{1}{6}\left[
\frac{6}{1-5/6}-\frac{1}{1-1/2}-\frac{1}{1-2/3}
\right] \\
&= \boxed{\frac{31}{6}\approx 5.167}.
\end{align*}
$$

A shorter check uses the same tail-sum formula directly at the stopping
time. The maximum exceeds $4$ precisely when a $5$ or $6$ appears before
the first $4$. Among $\{4,5,6\}$, each is equally likely to appear first,
so this probability is $2/3$. Similarly, the maximum exceeds $5$ when
a $6$ appears before the first $4$, with probability $1/2$. Therefore

$$
\mathbb{E}[S_\tau]
= 4+\mathbb{P}(S_\tau>4)+\mathbb{P}(S_\tau>5)
= 4+\frac{2}{3}+\frac{1}{2}
= \frac{31}{6}.
$$

## Numerical Check

```{python}
# Packages
import numpy as np

# Set random seed
rng = np.random.default_rng(seed=342)


# Single experiment iteration
def roll_until_4():
    test = False
    x = []
    s = []
    while test is False:
        roll = rng.integers(low=1, high=7)
        x.append(roll)
        s.append(np.max(np.array(x)))
        if roll == 4:
            test = True
    return np.array(x), np.array(s)


# Empirical mean
s_vals = []
for _ in range(10000):
    x, s = roll_until_4()
    s_vals.append(s[-1])

# Print the average
print("The expected value is: ", np.mean(s_vals, axis=0))
```
